subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Parietal Cortex and Spatial Attention
description: Learn The Parietal Cortex and Spatial Attention in one minute.

hook.text: Your eyes can point one direction while your attention secretly shifts somewhere else entirely.

buildup.text: Covert attention is steered by the parietal cortex. It moves a mental spotlight without moving your eyes.

discovery.text: Posner's cueing task proved it: valid cues speed responses even when eyes stay fixed on center.

twist.text: Damage to the right parietal lobe causes hemispatial neglect—patients ignore the entire left side of space.

climax.text: They eat food only from the right side of the plate and draw clocks with all numbers crammed right.

punchline.text: Lose one parietal lobe and half the world vanishes.

quiz.question: What does right parietal lobe damage cause?
options: Hemispatial neglect of the left side

details.summary: The parietal cortex guides where attention is directed in space. Damage to the right parietal lobe causes hemispatial neglect, where patients ignore the left side of the world entirely, not because they cannot see but because they cannot attend to it.
details.whyItMatters: Hemispatial neglect is one of the most dramatic demonstrations that attention and perception are separate processes. You can have perfect eyesight yet fail to perceive what you do not attend to.
takeaways: The parietal cortex directs spatial attention
Right parietal damage causes neglect of left space
Neglect proves that seeing requires attention, not just vision

faq.question: What does hemispatial neglect look like in daily life?
faq.answer: Patients may eat food from only the right side of a plate, shave only the right side of their face, or draw only the right half of a clock. They are unaware of the deficit and genuinely do not experience the left side of space.

faq.question: Is hemispatial neglect the same as being blind on one side?
faq.answer: No. In blindness, the sensory input is lost. In neglect, visual processing still occurs but attention fails to engage the affected side. Patients can sometimes respond to stimuli on the neglected side if strongly cued, proving the sensory pathway is intact.
